battle.name: 唐滅史朝義之戰
battle.brief: 安史之亂末年，史思明死於魏州，史朝義以范陽為都割據河北。寶應元年秋冬，朝廷以僕固懷恩、郭子儀為副元帥，分兵九道進討；廣德元年范陽易主，史朝義為部將所斬，河北諸州復歸於唐。卡面亞述長弓不在唐軍序列，其車上弓兵連續齊射的射速優勢，正是唐軍以蹶張弩掩護攻城而難以維持壓制的對照。

kit.name: 亞述長弓
kit.history: 亞述人靠弓和鐵的組合征服兩河流域。弓兵在車上射，車兵靠弓兵開路。

countries: 唐滅史朝義之戰是安史之亂的最後一役，交戰的兩方一邊是唐朝中央與河北各道的官軍系統，一邊是史思明死後由其長子史朝義接掌的范陽割據勢力。唐方的指揮中樞在京城：寶應元年（762）十一月代宗崩，皇太子邠王李適即位，是為德宗，改元廣德；討叛的兵權交給以僕固懷恩為副元帥、郭子儀為副元帥的河東行軍，內侍魚朝恩以觀軍容使身分監軍。行軍並非單一主力，而是分作九道，由河中、太原、朔方、魏州、義武等地的節度使各率本部及行營兵北上，糧秣由太倉與沿途州縣供給，回鶻牙帳借出的騎兵則是攻勢中的尖刀。叛方的結構簡陋得多：史朝義以范陽（幽州）為根據地，號令河北諸州，令其子史要求和屯守魏州，把契丹、奚人等外族當作外援；藩鎮化的州縣各自擁兵，表面上奉史朝義之號，實則各自打算，命令傳到魏州以下已不甚靈光。這種中樞虛弱、地方各自為政的狀態，是唐軍得以在數月之內瓦解整個割據的關鍵。
countriesEn: The war that destroyed Shi Chaoyi was the last campaign of the An Lushan rebellion, and the two sides were the Tang central government with the armies of the circuits of Hebei on one hand, and on the other the secessionist power centred on Fanyang that Shi Chaoyi, the eldest son of Shi Siming, had inherited. The Tang command centre was in the capital. In the eleventh month of the Bao Ying era, 762, Emperor Daizong died, the crown prince Prince Bin, Li Shi, succeeded him as Dezong, and the year was renamed Guangde. The war was entrusted to a Hebei command in which Pugu Huai'en was deputy commander in chief and Guo Ziyi was the other, while the eunuch Yu Chao'en, as Commissioner for the Inspection of the Troops, supervised the army on the court's behalf. The expedition did not consist of a single main force: it was divided into nine columns, each raised and led by the military governors of places such as Hezhong, Taiyuan, Shuofang, Weizhou and Yiwu together with their own units and the field camps, the grain coming from the imperial granaries and from the districts along the line, while the cavalry lent by the Uighur khaganate formed the spearhead of the offensive. The structure of the rebels was far cruder. Shi Chaoyi used Fanyang, that is Yizhou, as his base, claimed authority over the prefectures of Hebei, posted his son Shi Yaohe to hold Weizhou, and looked to the peoples outside the frontier, the Khitan and the Xi, for support. The militarised prefectures each kept their own troops; in name they obeyed Shi Chaoyi, in fact each pursued its own interest, and his orders had little force as far south as Weizhou. That weakness of the centre and that independence of the localities were the reason the Tang army could break up the whole secession within a few months.
people: 史朝義是史思明的長子，突厥人，生於寧夷郡。史思明在魏州被其子與部將所弒，權位由史朝義接掌，他自立為主，一面遣使向唐廷請降、把魏州以外的地盤交出，一面令其子史要求和屯守魏州，又與契丹、奚人暗通款曲，兩面下注。到最後他眾叛親離，退保范陽，為部下所執，傳首京師。執行此次討伐的僕固懷恩是河中同羅部落出身、歸唐後賜姓的宿將，他與史思明結怨多年，又感朝廷厚恩，於是主動請討，總攝河北行軍，並以回鶻援軍配合郭子儀所率的漢軍，攻城與野戰並進。郭子儀是本役中名望最重的老將，以持重知名，約束部曲不得剽掠，所過州縣多能望風歸順。監軍魚朝恩是內侍，與懷恩嫌隙頗深，事後更因私怨中傷懷恩。史朝義一方還有獨孤渾、岑奉元等人物：前者參與弒父而旋被猜忌，後者在范陽之變中扭轉了結局。河北各州的刺史與縣令多在關鍵時刻倒戈，他們的取捨決定了攻勢的快慢。
peopleEn: Shi Chaoyi was the eldest son of Shi Siming, a Turk born in Ningyi prefecture. Shi Siming was murdered at Weizhou by his son together with one of his commanders, and the position passed to Shi Chaoyi, who set up as ruler in his own right: he sent envoys to the Tang court to offer submission and handed over the ground outside Weizhou, while at the same time he posted his son Shi Yaohe to hold Weizhou, and he came to secret terms with the Khitan and the Xi, betting in two directions at once. In the end his followers fell away, he withdrew to Fanyang, and he was taken by his own men and his head was carried to the capital. The man who carried out the campaign, Pugu Huai'en, was an old commander of Huguodu descent from the Tongluo tribe of Hezhong, who had been given the surname Pugu after submitting to the Tang. He had long-standing grudges against Shi Siming and felt deep gratitude to the court, so he volunteered to take the field, took charge of the Hebei expedition, and combined the Uighur auxiliaries with the Chinese army of Guo Ziyi, mixing siege operations with open battle. Guo Ziyi was the commander of greatest renown in the campaign, famous for his caution and for holding his men to their discipline, so that the districts through which he passed often submitted at his approach. The Supervisor of the Troops, Yu Chao'en, was a eunuch, and he and Huai'en were on bad terms; afterwards he made it his business to slander Huai'en out of private spite. On Shi Chaoyi's side there were men such as Dugu Hun and Cen Fengyuan: the first had a hand in the murder of the father and was distrusted soon after, and the second turned the course of events at Fanyang. The prefects and county magistrates of the Hebei districts turned their coats at the decisive moments, and their choices determined how fast the offensive moved.
kits: 卡面這把亞述長弓（Assyrian bow）本身不會出現在762年的河北戰場上，把它放進來是因為它標示的是一條技術譜系。亞述長弓是木胎、內貼牛角、外纏筋腱的複合反曲弓，張距短而箭速高，亞述人把它裝上車陣：弓兵站在車上發射，車兵靠弓兵開路，靠弓與鐵的組合走遍兩河流域。唐代的弓正是這條譜系的東端延伸：弓胎以竹木為骨，內襯角片、外蒙皮並髹漆，同樣是複合反曲，同樣以短張距換取箭速。戰場上真正大量消耗的還有弩：蹶張弩以人力張弦，每發都須重新上弦，連續壓制的節奏因此受限，單兵弩配箭袋，床子弩架在車上施放，都是唐軍對付城池與密集人馬的手段；亞述車上弓兵每車一人可連續齊射，車隊便靠這份持續火力開路，兩種射速的差距正是本役攻城節奏的關鍵。防具方面有明光甲、皂縞甲與札甲，騎兵多披半臂或只穿綿甲；盾以櫓木為主，拒馬用於封堵城門與道路。攻城器械包括巢車、雲梯、破城車與砲車，遠程火力之外還有火箭一類的燃燒器材，唐人丹經中已見火硝火藥的記載，但冷兵器與弓弩仍是作戰主幹。河北叛軍以遊牧騎兵為骨幹，契丹、奚人用的是便於騎射的小弓，攻城時則雜用步卒與臨時器械。馬匹是此役真正的瓶頸：河中與河西的蕃馬、回鶻借來的健騎，構成追擊與突破的速度；糧車與黃河、汴河的水運則是維持這支騎兵在千里戰線上作戰的關鍵。
kitsEn: The Assyrian bow on the card would not itself have been present on a battlefield in Hebei in 762, and it is placed here because it marks a line of technical descent. The Assyrian bow is a composite recurve of a wooden core lined with horn on the inside and bound with sinew on the outside; it has a short draw and a high arrow speed, and the Assyrians mounted it on vehicles: the archers shot from the carts, and the charioteers relied on the archers to open the way, and it was this combination of the bow and iron that carried them through the two river valleys. The Tang bow was the far eastern continuation of that same line: its belly was built on bamboo and wood, lined with horn, covered with hide and lacquered, composite and recurve in just the same way, and it bought the same arrow speed with the same short draw. What was consumed in far greater numbers on the battlefield was the crossbow. There were the drawing crossbow worked by the strength of a man, the single-man crossbow with its quiver, and the bed crossbow mounted on a cart, all of them the Tang answer to walls and to massed men. For protection there were the Mingguang harness, the Zao'e harness and the lamellar armour, while the cavalry often wore only half-armour or padded jacks; the shield was the wooden pavise, and the horse-fence was used to block gates and roads. The siege equipment included the scaling tower, the siege ladder, the battering cart and the stone-thrower, and beside the long-range artillery there were burning projectiles of the rocket kind; the alchemical texts of the Tang already record saltpetre and gunpowder, yet cold weapons, the bow and the crossbow remained the trunk of the fighting. The rebel army of Hebei was built on its nomadic cavalry, and the Khitan and the Xi used the short bows that are workable from the saddle, while for sieges they made do with foot soldiers and improvised engines. Horses were the real bottleneck of the campaign: the horses of the western districts, the strong mounts lent by the Uighur, gave the speed needed for pursuit and for breaking through; and the grain carts and the water transport of the Yellow River and of the Bian canal were what kept that cavalry supplied along a front of a thousand li.
tactics: 唐廷沒有把希望寄在一次會戰上，而是以多路進逼與政治招撫並行。開戰前，朝廷以詔書宣諭河北諸州，凡能反正者官復舊職、家產不追，把史朝義的部眾同河北州縣的本地力量分開；同時分兵九道，自河中、太原等處東出，取井陘等太行陘道壓向河北平原，避免走同一條運糧大道，減少補給被截斷的機會。前段的重點是魏州：史要求和據城拒守，唐軍一面攻城，一面策動城中反正，最終史要求和為部下所殺，魏州城隨之而下，這一步打開了河北南部的門戶。中段在河北平原上展開騎兵戰：僕固懷恩以回鶻騎兵為鋒，郭子儀部漢軍隨之，叛軍本無集中的大軍，各州守兵多各自求戰，防線在幾次遭遇中被逐段咬開。末段是范陽：史朝義本可據堅城固守，但他自度眾心已散，先期退保范陽，幽州守軍隨即開城或反正，叛軍的最後據點自行崩解，兵馬器械散於郊野。追擊階段，回鶻騎兵疾行數百里，截斷潰兵與糧道；郭子儀一路約束部眾安集州縣、復置官吏，唐廷的影響力於是由河北中南部重新長回幽州。戰役自寶應元年秋冬的出兵算起，到廣德元年正月范陽易主，前後不過三四個月，是唐廷用最少的時間結束八年亂局的一次總攻。
tacticsEn: The Tang court did not pin its hopes on a single pitched battle; it advanced on several axes at once while opening a political front as well. Before the fighting began, edicts went out to the prefectures of Hebei promising that all who came over would have their offices restored and their property left untouched, in order to separate Shi Chaoyi's own followers from the local strength of the Hebei districts. At the same time the army was split into nine columns advancing east from Hezhong, Taiyuan and other bases, taking the passes of the Taihang range such as Jingxing down onto the plain of Hebei, so as not to crowd onto the single great grain road and to reduce the chance of the supplies being cut. The weight of the first phase fell on Weizhou. Shi Yaohe held the city and refused terms, and the Tang army besieged it while working on the defenders inside; in the end Shi Yaohe was killed by his own men and Weizhou fell with him, which opened the southern gate of Hebei. The middle phase was fought as a cavalry war on the plain: Pugu Huai'en led with the Uighur horsemen and Guo Ziyi's Chinese troops followed, for the rebels had no massed army, the garrisons of the different prefectures fought their own separate actions, and the line was bitten away piece by piece in a series of encounters. The last phase was Fanyang. Shi Chaoyi might have held behind his strong walls, but he judged that his followers were already gone, fell back on Fanyang in advance, and the troops of Youzhou there either opened the gates or came over, so that the last strongpoint of the rebellion collapsed of itself, its men and its weapons scattering over the fields. In pursuit the Uighur horsemen rode hard for several hundred li, cutting off the broken troops and the grain route; and Guo Ziyi kept his men in hand all the way, settling the districts and reinstating the officers, so that the authority of the Tang court grew back from the centre and south of Hebei to Yizhou. Counting from the dispatch of the columns in the last months of the Bao Ying era to the change of Fanyang in the first month of Guangde, the whole campaign took no more than three or four months: it was the general assault by which the Tang court ended eight years of disorder in the shortest possible time.
data: 可核對的數字分三類。系年最為明確：史思明死於761年，史朝義在范陽立事；寶應元年（762）九月僕固懷恩自吐蕃還朝請討，十月朝廷命懷恩為副元帥、郭子儀為副元帥、魚朝恩為觀軍容使，分兵九道；十一月代宗崩，邠王李適即位改元廣德；廣德元年正月，范陽易主，史朝義死。部分系年把范陽之滅繫於763年正月，蓋因唐代改元常在年內，寶應元年十二月即改稱廣德元年正月，兩種寫法指的是同一件事。兵員方面，總數在傳世文獻中不見明文，只留下分兵九道、各道自本部出兵的記載，故只能推估全軍當在數萬至十萬的量級，其中回鶻借出的騎兵為數千之眾；河北叛軍沒有可計的常備兵，各州兵與遊牧騎兵分屬不同首領，實際集結數量遠低於唐方。城池與州縣數量上，河北自趙州、深州、魏州、德州到恆、邢、洺一線的州縣多在半年內相繼歸唐，幽州為最後一處。里程方面，由魏州至范陽的軍路約六百餘里，騎兵疾行十日可至，糧車則需月餘，沿線設驛與屯積軍糧是行軍的依賴。兵器方面，亞述複合弓的考古推定張距約六十至七十公分上下，箭鏃多見鐵、骨、石三類，這是比較古今弓具時常用的參照，但與唐弩的實際規格不可直接換算。傷亡與損耗沒有可核實的數字：史書多以眾潰、兵散、器械盡棄概之，只記叛軍首級傳至京師，而不載雙方精確死傷；唐軍的消耗主要在疲乏與運糧，而不在任何一場會戰。
dataEn: The numbers that can be checked fall into three classes. The chronology is the clearest. Shi Siming died in 761 and Shi Chaoyi took up his position at Fanyang; in the ninth month of the Bao Ying era, 762, Pugu Huai'en returned to court from the Tibetan side and asked to campaign against him; in the tenth month the court appointed Huai'en and Guo Ziyi as deputy commanders in chief and Yu Chao'en as Commissioner for the Inspection of the Troops, and divided the force into nine columns; in the eleventh month Daizong died, the Prince of Bin, Li Shi, succeeded him and the era was renamed Guangde; and in the first month of Guangde Fanyang changed hands and Shi Chaoyi died. Some chronologies place the fall of Fanyang in the first month of 763, because in the Tang the renaming of the year commonly took place within the year, the twelfth month of Bao Ying being at once renamed the first month of Guangde, so the two reckonings describe the same event. As for numbers of troops, no clear figure survives in the transmitted texts, which record only the division into nine columns and the fact that each marched with its own units, so the whole force can only be estimated at a level of tens of thousands up to a hundred thousand, of which the cavalry lent by the Uighur was some thousands strong. The rebel army of Hebei had no countable standing force: the troops of the prefectures and the nomadic horsemen belonged to different leaders, and the strength they could actually bring together was far below that of the Tang side. As for the number of cities and districts, the prefectures of Hebei from the line of Zhaozhou, Shenzhou, Weizhou and Dezhou through Hengzhou, Xingzhou and Mingzhou came over to the Tang one after another within half a year, with Youzhou the last of them. As for distances, the military road from Weizhou to Fanyang ran to something over six hundred li; horsemen riding hard could do it in ten days, while the grain carts needed a month or more, and the relay stations and the stockpiling of military grain along the line were what the marching depended on. As for arms, the archaeological estimate for the draw of the Assyrian composite bow is a matter of sixty to seventy centimetres or so, and arrowheads are found in iron, bone and stone; these are the usual points of reference when comparing bows across the ages, though they cannot be converted directly into the specifications of a Tang crossbow. There are no verifiable figures for losses. The histories summarise the end in a few words, the host dispersed, the weapons thrown away, and record only that the head of the rebel was carried to the capital, without giving precise losses for either side. The Tang losses were spent mainly on exhaustion and on the carriage of grain, and not in any single pitched battle.
cause: 打起來的起因有遠有近。遠因是安史之亂八年之後河北的割據格局：史思明在世時以幽州、魏州兩地為樞軸，把河北州縣的軍鎮化狀態推到頂點；他一死，留給兒子的是一個中樞虛弱、地方各自為政的聯盟，中間卻沒有能壓得住局面的人。直接導火線是史朝義的兩面手法：他一面遣使請降，把魏州以外的城邑交出，一面令史要求和屯守魏州，又與契丹、奚人續立舊盟，逼近幽州南面；朝廷在代宗新喪之際無法接受一個仍握重兵、仍能聯絡外族的藩鎮，於是放棄招撫，改以兵力解決。推動此役的關鍵人物是僕固懷恩：他自吐蕃返回朝廷，見河北有機可乘，便上表請討，願以河中兵為先部，並借回鶻兵以速戰勝；朝廷正需要一位在河朔有戰功、又與回鶻可通消息的統帥，於是全盤依其方略。還有更深的一層：吐蕃在西北牽制，唐廷無法在此時對河北用兵拖延，一旦開打就必須速勝；安史之亂中唐廷屢戰屢敗的教訓，使它寧可集中十萬之眾打一次殲滅戰，也不肯再打持久戰。
causeEn: The reasons for the war are both immediate and remote. The remote reason is the secessionary pattern that had grown across Hebei in the eight years since the rebellion began. While Shi Siming lived, the pivot of the region was the pair of places, Youzhou and Weizhou, and he had pushed the militarisation of the Hebei prefectures to its extreme. When he died he left his son a coalition with a hollow centre and localities each following their own road, and no one in the middle capable of holding it together. The immediate spark was the two-faced conduct of Shi Chaoyi. He sent envoys to offer submission and handed over the cities outside Weizhou, and at the same time he posted Shi Yaohe to hold Weizhou, and he renewed the old compact with the Khitan and the Xi, pressing close to the south of Youzhou. The court, newly bereaved of Emperor Daizong, could not accept a provincial governor who still held heavy troops and still corresponded with peoples beyond the frontier, and so it gave up the policy of pacification and settled the matter by force. The man who drove the campaign was Pugu Huai'en. He had come back to court from the Tibetan side, saw that an opportunity had opened in Hebei, and thereupon memorialised for a campaign, offering the troops of Hezhong as the vanguard and asking to borrow Uighur horsemen so as to win quickly. The court needed a commander who had fought in the lands north of the Yellow River and who could keep in touch with the Uighur, and so it followed his plan in full. There is a deeper layer still. The Tibetans were tying down the north-west, and the Tang court could not afford to bog down its operations in Hebei; once the fighting began it had to be won quickly. The lesson of the repeated defeats of the Tang in the course of the rebellion was that it would rather concentrate a hundred thousand men on a single campaign of annihilation than fight one more war of attrition.
impact: 這一役的直接後果是安史之亂的終結。763年河北諸州盡復於唐，唐朝第二次收復兩京之後維持了八年的割據狀態宣告結束，杜甫聞訊寫下『劍外忽傳收薊北，初聞涕淚滿衣裳』，成為文獻上對這場戰爭最著名的標記。但勝利的代價與隱患同時浮現。河北經年戰亂之後州縣殘破、倉廩空虛，唐廷重設州縣、復置官吏所需的錢糧，遠超戰時的軍費；國庫因此更加吃緊，同年吐蕃趁朝廷新喪與河北疲敝之際大舉入寇，一度攻入長安，唐廷被迫再次遷都、募兵，亂局並未真正收束。制度上，叛軍降將被大量授以節度使職，河北形成成德、魏博、盧龍等鎮，河朔三鎮的格局由此定型，中央對邊防與財政的調度能力卻被削弱；安史之亂前尚能調度府兵的老框架已崩，募兵與長駐邊軍成為常態，藩鎮的財政與兵權自此難以回收。僕固懷恩的結局尤其值得記取：他以破史朝義之功自恃，與監軍魚朝恩嫌隙日深，763年又與吐蕃陰謀內應，事發而死於軍中，所部隨即由郭子儀收拾。討平史朝義的將軍幾乎立刻變成新的亂源，這正是唐代中期政治最沉痛的循環。
impactEn: The direct consequence of this campaign was the end of the An Lushan rebellion. In 763 the prefectures of Hebei were all restored to the Tang, the state of secession that had lasted eight years after the second recovery of the two capitals was declared over, and Du Fu, on hearing the news, wrote that the news of recovering Jibei came suddenly to him beyond the Sword Gate and that at first hearing his tears filled his garments, which remains the most famous mark in the literature on this war. But the cost of the victory and its hidden dangers appeared at the same time. After years of war the prefectures of Hebei lay ruined and the granaries empty, and the money and grain needed to re-establish the districts and reinstate the officers far exceeded the expenses of the campaign itself. The treasury was tightened accordingly, and in the same year the Tibetans, taking advantage of the new mourning at court and of the exhaustion of Hebei, invaded in force and for a time occupied the capital of Chang'an, so that the Tang court was driven to move the capital once more and to raise new troops; the disorder was not truly wound up. Institutionally, the rebel commanders who came over were given command posts in large numbers, and in Hebei the circuits of Chengde, Weibo and Lulong took shape, so that the pattern of the three circuits north of the Yellow River was fixed, while the capacity of the centre to direct the frontier and the finances was weakened. The old framework that could still dispatch the fubing before the rebellion had already collapsed, levies and long-service frontier troops became the norm, and from then on the money and the troops of the provincial commands were not recoverable. The fate of Pugu Huai'en is especially worth recording. Elated by the credit for destroying Shi Chaoyi, he grew ever more hostile to the Supervisor Yu Chao'en, and in 763 he entered into a secret Understanding with the Tibetans for a rising inside the empire; the plot came to light and he died in the camp, and his troops were then taken in hand by Guo Ziyi. The general who had destroyed Shi Chaoyi very nearly became at once the source of a new disorder, and that is the most painful cycle of Tang politics in the middle ages.
result: 廣德元年正月，史朝義在眾叛親離中退保范陽，為部下所執，傳首京師，河北最後的割據中樞垮掉。同一段時間裡，魏州、趙州、深州、德州、恆州、邢州、洺州等河北州縣相繼反正，幽州歸唐，安史之亂至此完全平定。朝廷隨即詔令宣慰河北各州，復舊官吏、罷進奉、止括兵，安置降附軍隊，並以范陽為治重設幽州防務，以防契丹、奚人再度南下。戰果是明確的：延續八年的內亂以一次成功的總攻收場，唐朝恢復了對河北平原的名義控制，國家的兵馬與政令重新覆蓋到幽州城下。但這場勝利並沒有解決問題的根源。河北的藩鎮化已難以逆轉，降將與叛軍殘部被編入唐軍體系，成德、魏博、盧龍等鎮取得兵權與財權，與中央形成長期僵持；郭子儀在河北所保留下來的軍鎮，幾乎在二十餘年後就成為再度割據的源頭。僕固懷恩的驕橫與反叛，讓朝廷在勝利的同時又面對新的軍事危機；而同年吐蕃的入侵把首都置於危亡，更證明這場平叛的成果脆弱。史朝義的覆亡給唐廷帶來了喘息的空間，卻沒有帶來解決的方案——安史之亂結束了，割據的時代才剛剛開始。
resultEn: In the first month of Guangde, Shi Chaoyi, deserted by his followers, fell back on Fanyang, was taken by his own men, and his head was carried to the capital; the last secessionary centre in Hebei collapsed. Within the same stretch of time the prefectures of Hebei, Weizhou, Zhaozhou, Shenzhou, Dezhou, Hengzhou, Xingzhou, Mingzhou and the rest, came over one after another, Youzhou returned to the Tang, and the An Lushan rebellion was completely wound up. The court then issued edicts to pacify the prefectures of Hebei, restoring the old officers, calling off the levies of tribute, stopping the mustering of men, settling the surrendered troops, and re-establishing the defence of Youzhou with its seat at Fanyang against any renewed descent by the Khitan and the Xi. The result is plain: an internal disorder that had run for eight years was closed out by a single successful general assault, and the Tang recovered nominal control of the plain of Hebei, the soldiers and the ordinances of the state once more reaching the walls of Youzhou. But the victory did not reach the root of the trouble. The militarisation of Hebei could no longer be reversed; rebel commanders and the remnants of the rebel forces were taken into the Tang army system, and the circuits of Chengde, Weibo and Lulong obtained both the right of the sword and the right of the purse, standing in long standoff with the centre. The garrisons that Guo Ziyi had preserved in Hebei were, in little more than twenty years, to become the source of a fresh secession. The arrogance and the rebellion of Pugu Huai'en meant that the court, in the very same moment of victory, was faced with a new military crisis; and the Tibetan invasion of that year, which put the capital itself in danger, showed only too well how fragile the results of this pacification were. The fall of Shi Chaoyi gave the Tang court room to draw breath, but it brought no solution: the An Lushan rebellion was over, and the age of the provincial commands had only just begun.
